blocks.x: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance — an Achala packaged solution: a named business problem, a composed architecture from two to four service domains, and a value case written in units a CFO recognizes. Sized and piloted in weeks, measured on the metric it exists to move.
Assets run to failure on calendar PMs; telemetry exists but doesn't reach planning; predictions that aren't trusted get ignored.
Beneath the symptom in Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance sits the same defect everywhere: judgment work trapped inside manual assembly. The composition below is the way out.

We instrument the failure modes that pay, build physics-informed RUL models validated on work-order history, wire predictions into EAM/CMMS scheduling with parts staging, and manage false-alarm discipline as a first-class metric.
In Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance, the components, as they land:

items: predictions to scheduled work with parts
downtime hours, cost per unit, trust rate

blocks.x: Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance composes BI & Analytics Platform, EEMS Platform, platforms with documented controls and evidence packs, so governance is part of the runtime. The pattern is in delivery now in Manufacturing & Industrial, Energy & Utilities, Logistics & Supply Chain, Retail & Consumer Goods.

Method over magic in Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance: the problem gets a CFO-unit statement and a signed baseline; the design gets a written risk envelope; the pilot gets falsifiable criteria; the rollout gets whatever the evidence supports. In Predictive Maintenance & Asset Performance programs the same rule applies: what we promise is modest and checkable: a signed baseline, a bounded slice in production, and evidence your auditors can read without a guide.
What your control owner sees weekly
